chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghayath from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Monopoly (Hukrah) is not [permitted] except in wheat, barley, dates, raisins, and ghee."

key_terms.الْحُكْرَةُ: Monopoly; the act of buying up a commodity to control its price or supply

ai.seo_question: Which specific commodities are subject to the ruling of Hukrah (monopoly) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that the prohibition of *Hukrah* (monopolizing essential goods to manipulate prices) is strictly limited to five staple commodities: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, and ghee. This limitation reflects the Shia juristic view that the ruling applies primarily to basic sustenance items critical for public welfare, distinguishing them from other goods where market dynamics may differ. The narration underscores the economic justice principles central to Shia fiqh, ensuring that essential food supplies remain accessible to the general populace.
